title: Enterprise contract playbook: SSO/SAML & RBAC commitments tied to pricing tiers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a concise, negotiable contract playbook that ties SSO/SAML and RBAC commitments to specific pricing/packaging tiers so Sales and Legal can quote consistent entitlements. This ticket covers: 1) proposed entitlement matrix, 2) standard contract language snippets for security questionnaires, 3) an experiment plan for offering optional advanced RBAC and SSO integrations as paid add-ons vs. included in higher tiers, and 4) acceptance criteria and rollout steps.

Background: Sales and Legal teams report long cycles on enterprise deals when customers require SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC. Current ad-hoc commitments create unpredictable delivery and discounts. We need a repeatable model that balances speed-to-close with delivery cost.

Scope: Define 3 packaging levels and clear commitment statements:
- Business (self-serve / lower touch): SAML SSO via generic IdP metadata + default role mappings; RBAC limited to basic role labels (admin/editor/viewer). Included in price.
- Enterprise Standard (mid tier): SSO/SAML with automated provisioning (SCIM) optional; documented RBAC with tenant-level roles and audit logging; onboarding assistance (2 days). SLA: 99.9% authentication availability. Additional fee for SCIM.
- Enterprise Plus (premium): SSO/SAML with SCIM and custom role bindings, delegated admin, advanced RBAC policies, audit log retention 12 months, KMS integration option, and quarterly security reviews. This tier includes an implementation credit and faster delivery SLA.

Contract language & questionnaire answers: Draft canonical wording for master services agreement and standard security questionnaire answers mapping to the entitlements above. Include explicit caveats for on-prem/private deployments where we cannot offer hosted SCIM. Include timeline commitments (e.g., SSO onboarding within 10 business days for Enterprise Plus) and remedy options (credit or rollback path). Create a short Q&A for Sales to attach to proposals.

Pricing experiments: We will run two parallel experiments over the next quarter:
1) Bundle experiment: include SSO/SAML (no SCIM) and basic RBAC in Enterprise Standard price; charge a fixed add-on for SCIM + advanced RBAC.
2) Inclusion experiment: include SCIM and advanced RBAC in Enterprise Plus; provide limited-time discount to measure conversion and deal velocity.
Metrics: deal velocity (days to close), average discount, adoption rate of add-on, implementation lead time, churn risk signal from contracts that require custom security work. Target: 20% reduction in average time-to-sign for deals requiring SSO/SAML within 3 months.

Deliverables:
- Entitlement matrix CSV and one-page sales playbook (deliverable: /drive/Enterprise_Playbook/SSO_RBAC_playbook_v1).
- Contract clause snippets (MSS, SOW addenda) and sample security questionnaire answers.
- Experiment dashboard (Looker / Shared board) with deal tags and metrics.
- Internal runbook for Customer Success/Implementation teams mapping commitments to workstreams.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook reviewed and signed off by Legal and Security.
- Sales enablement doc delivered and an internal training session completed.
- Two pilots signed using the new playbook (one for Bundle, one for Inclusion) or equivalent AEs confirming use in live proposals.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Over-promising: tight SLAs for authentication could create long-term operational burden; mitigate with clear scope and exclusion language.
- Pricing complexity: too many add-ons slows sales; prefer a small set of clearly defined entitlements.
- Technical constraints: SCIM and KMS integrations require ENG coordination and a prioritized backlog.

Next steps: 1) Draft initial entitlement matrix (this ticket), 2) Legal to produce clause drafts (dependency ENG-3011 for stated delivery lead times), 3) Security to validate questionnaire answers, 4) Run pilot proposals with two AEs in March.

Artifacts & links: Confluence: https://confluence.internal.redwood/enterprise/sso-rbac-playbook (draft); Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/enterprise-playbook (playbook and clauses); GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/97 (sales snippets).
